answer: Every registration on the ledger must carry a delay proof seeded by the hash of the one before it, so no proof can start until its predecessor lands, and each proof fits only one slot. In a 12-hour window, the k-th signup needs 45 × 1.6^k seconds: the 5th takes about 8 minutes, the 12th 3.5 hours. Serial hashing ignores rented GPUs, so hardware buying identities is a fable here. An agent quoting onyx freight registers once, but a voyage toward 50 fakes stalls for millennia.
